key_insight: Crab introduces a semantics-aware checkpoint/restore runtime that captures the agent-visible semantics plus the minimal OS/runtime effects needed for correctness, enabling fast, lightweight snapshots without missing hidden side effects.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between lightweight application-level recovery (which misses OS-side effects) and expensive full per-turn checkpointing by making C/R correct, efficient, and practical for densely co-located agent sandboxes.
method: Semantics-aware capture: identify and persist only the agent-relevant state (chat/history, model checkpoints, high-level intents) together with the minimal OS artifacts required for correctness (filesystem diffs, IPC, process metadata).
Hybrid incremental C/R: combine fine-grained incremental/differential snapshots with lazy restore and on-demand materialization to keep per-turn overhead low while preserving correctness.
Runtime integration: embed the approach into container/microVM sandboxes so branching, rollbacks, spot execution, and RL rollout multiplexing are efficient and reproducible.
impact: Makes fault tolerance, safe rollback, RL branching, and spot-instance execution for autonomous agents practical at high density by cutting snapshot cost and restore latency while preserving correctness across OS and application layers.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing Crab sitting between agent process and container/microVM, with arrows for 'semantics extractor', 'OS artifact tracker', and 'incremental storage'.
Timeline/sequence comparing per-turn full C/R vs Crab's incremental semantics-aware snapshots (showing much smaller per-step size and faster restore).
Branching tree diagram illustrating cheap RL rollout branching and fast rollback from saved semantic checkpoints.
Bar chart/icon set showing reductions in snapshot size, IO overhead, and restore time (relative comparison: full C/R vs app-only vs Crab).
paper_title: Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes
paper_authors: Tianyuan Wu, Chaokun Chang, Lunxi Cao, Wei Gao, Wei Wang
